title: Customer signs in to their own account

card.i_want: to sign in with my email and password and receive a session
card.so_that: I can reach my own cart, addresses and orders and nobody else's

intent: Customers stop depending on staff to identify them, and every later own-data-only check has an identity to enforce against.

acceptance_criteria.scenario_name: customer signs in with valid credentials
given: a registered customer with a verified email and the correct password
acceptance_criteria.when: the customer submits the sign-in form
then: an access token valid for 15 minutes and a refresh token valid for 14 days are issued
the customer reaches their own cart and order list

acceptance_criteria.scenario_name: an unknown email and a wrong password are indistinguishable
given: one sign-in attempt for an email that has no account
one sign-in attempt for a real account with the wrong password
then: both responses carry the identical message and the identical status
neither response reveals whether the email exists

acceptance_criteria.scenario_name: the access token expires exactly at its lifetime
given: an access token issued 15 minutes ago
acceptance_criteria.when: the customer calls an authenticated endpoint
then: the request is refused as expired
the same call one minute earlier would have succeeded

acceptance_criteria.scenario_name: a password never appears in any output
given: any sign-in attempt, successful or failed
then: no log line, response body or error trace contains the submitted password
the stored value is a one-way hash that cannot be reversed

acceptance_criteria.scenario_name: only the owning customer's data is reachable with the issued token
given: customer A signed in and holding a valid access token
acceptance_criteria.when: customer A requests customer B's cart
then: no field of customer B's data appears in the response

pii_fields.justification: the sign-in identifier is the customer email, a direct identifier
pii_fields.treatment: redacted in logs; domain only in admin lists

audit_events.justification: authentication outcomes are security events that must be attributable

idempotency.justification: sign-in is a read-shaped authentication with no state a repeat could duplicate

reversibility.justification: issuing a session moves no money and writes no external state

authn_authz.justification: this story IS the authentication boundary every later own-data check depends on

regulatory.justification: PDPA B.E. 2562 s24 governs the credential and the email as contract-basis personal data

tipping_off.justification: no financial-crime context; the identical-message rule is anti-enumeration, not anti-tipping-off

edge_case_ledger.justification: token expiry is evaluated per request against a single clock, so no two actors contend and no second system of record is written
a repeated failed sign-in produces the same refusal with no state to duplicate
a one-way hash has no numeric boundary to sit at
